item.description: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay on Friday following the impeachment of his predecessor over a massive banking crisis that locked almost half the country out of their accounts. Senators appointed Alliana, the former vice president, shortly after voting to remove Santiago Pena over the chaotic collapse of a bank to which he had links. Senate President Basilio Nunez declared Pena “guilty of poor performance in his duties” after 44 out of 45 senators voted in favor of impeachment, with one lawmaker absent. Hundreds of people waiting outside Congress raucously celebrated his impeachment. “Justice has been done. Now we want him to give us back our money and go to jail,” Jessica Aquino, 32, told AFP. Paraguayan authorities placed the ex-leader under house arrest minutes after his removal, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester told reporters. item.title: Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory
item.description: The mayor of Houston, Texas announced Friday that the city’s police department will limit its cooperation with federal immigration agents after Democrats swept midterm elections this week. The so-called “blue tsunami” ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Texas ally of US President Donald Trump, who has cracked down on immigration with raids conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents since returning to office last year. Abbott had threatened in April to revoke $110 million in public safety funding from Houston if city officials didn’t walk back a similar measure earlier this year, and city officials complied. He lost reelection on Tuesday and will be replaced by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, the first Latina woman elected governor of Texas. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire has signed an executive order instructing Houston police to not contact ICE agents when a person is detained for nonviolent offenses, like a traffic stop. “It’s to reduce the fear and anxiety, not just in some of our communities but across Houston,” Whitmire said during a press conference announcing the change. The 77-year-old mayor acknowledged that the change could bring some political risks but said he was ready to meet them, as Abbott and other Republicans remain in power until January. ICE released a statement on X reacting to the change, writing: “Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as ‘nonviolent offenses’ by the way.” “This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America,” it added. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, a nonpartisan think tank, Texas has had more arrests carried out by ICE agents during Trump’s second term than any other state, with almost 137,000 recorded as of August 2026. Texas is also the state with the highest number of ICE detainees in the US, with over 16,000 held at various facilities — more than double the amount held in the second highest state, Louisiana — according to Syracuse University’s Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. item.title: How pregnant woman delivered inside Danfo in Lagos
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Passengers inside a commercial bus, popularly called Danfo in Lagos were stunned when a fellow passenger suddenly went into sudden labor and successfully gave birth to a baby boy on board. According to Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the woman was traveling across the state when labor began unexpectedly mid-journey In the process, fellow commuters and onlookers quickly assisted her through the delivery inside the vehicle while others went into prayer session for safe delivery. Medical responders and local commuters assisted in securing the mother and child immediately following the emergency delivery. Fortunately, after few minutes, the baby boy was delivered safely. In viral footage capturing the moments following the birth, witnesses suggested naming the child Abiona—a traditional Yoruba name commonly associated with a child born on a journey or along the road. Recall that a similar incident happened at Onipanu Bus Stop, along Ikorodu Road sometimes ago. “In a swift r​esponse, LASEMA arrived at the scene to assist a pregnant woman who went into sudden labor while waiting for transport. “The woman delivered a healthy baby boy. Both mother and child were stabilized by LASEMA paramedics before being transported to a nearby healthcare facility for post-natal care,” LASEMA Permanent Secretary, Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu stated. Legally, public assurances cannot settle the status of a nomination. The subsidy proposal also deserves close questioning. What would be subsidised? Who would benefit? Atiku is trying to prevent legal uncertainty from becoming political demobilisation. His next consequential development will be an authoritative court decision or INEC action, rather than another declaration that he will contest. Experience deserves examination through results. Promises deserve examination through funding and implementation. The useful comparisons concern access to work, education and training; the cost of starting a business; reliable electricity; personal safety; and the ability to participate in politics without intimidation. A separate development today also draws attention to young Nigerians as election workers. Governor Seyi Makinde urged corps members to remain impartial during electoral duties, while a corps member called for adequate security. Their responsibilities make youth participation an issue of electoral administration as well as voting preference. Youth Metre assessment No verified shift in candidate preference established today. Claims that a candidate has captured or lost the youth vote need evidence beyond speeches, rally pictures and social media reaction. Today’s campaigning invites a comparison of records. The candidates should welcome the same scrutiny they demand of their opponents. The strongest campaign will connect an account of past performance with a believable answer to the voter’s next question: what will improve in my life if you win? item.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
item.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. In another significant outcome, Israel’s Mr. Shai Mazai secured 134 votes to emerge as the recommended candidate from the Group of Western European and Other States to the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee subsequently recommended his appointment to the committee for a three-year term, also beginning January 1, 2027. The elections formed part of the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119, which covers appointments to fill vacancies in subsidiary organs and other appointments. Other bodies considered during the exercise included the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee on Contributions and the Investment Committee, alongside the International Civil Service Commission and the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee, chaired by Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, also recommended candidates from other regional groups to the International Civil Service Commission through acclamation, following the absence of contested nominations for the respective seats. At the conclusion of the exercise, Ambassador Ibrahim commended delegates for their patience, cooperation and commitment throughout the electoral process. He also congratulated those recommended for appointment and urged them to uphold the integrity of the Fifth Committee while discharging their responsibilities. The Nigerian diplomat equally acknowledged the contributions of the tellers and officials nominated by Member States to supervise the electoral process. Ambassador Ibrahim subsequently declared the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119 concluded and requested the Rapporteur to communicate its decisions to the General Assembly for further action. item.description: Within a span of one week, opposition political parties in Nigeria have experienced various challenges in their bid to contest in the 2027 general elections. According to the report, after a search warrant was conducted in the house and premises of the suspects, some relevant Jaiz Bank documents were recovered from her possession. It added that investigation activities were communicated to Jaiz Bank, requesting for a comprehensive bank statement of the principal suspect and that of her husband, as well as one Muhammed Buhari Suleiman, who allegedly granted the principal suspect consent to use his corporate account to hide the money. “The principal suspect, Habiba Abdulrahman, was an employee and senior staff of the bank who betrayed the trust of the bank and that of customers. “Habiba Abdulrahman (suspect) engaged herself in fraudulent activities in the bank by obtaining money from some customers of Jaiz Bank Plc, Jos branch under a false pretence of opening fixed deposit account for them after making them fill and sign an account opening mandate. “Habiba Abdulrahman (suspect) engaged some bank customers, namely, Abdullahi Danasabe (m); Abubakar Yahaya Yunus (m); Hadiza Ishaku Garba (f); Zulail Danladi (f); Amina Inuwa Sa’ad (f); Odokor Amina Peace (f) and Hajara Ahmed (f). It was further discovered that the fixed deposit certificate Habiba issued to some customers was fake as the bank confirmed it to be forged documents. Habiba also used an Opay account belonging to Zainab Abdulrahman, who is her sister, to hide proceeds of the money from customers’ various accounts. “Therefore, it is suggested that Habiba Abdulrahman be charged to court for criminal conspiracy, breach of trust, forgery and cheating, while Munir Murtala and Zainab Abdulrahman should be charged for criminal conspiracy, receiving stolen property and abetment,” findings and report by the police stated. item.title: Anambra will deliver over 50% of 2027 votes to Tinubu — Soludo
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has promised to deliver at least 50 percent of the state’s votes to President Bola Tinubu, the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the 2027 general elections. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ The governor made the declaration during the flag off of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) 2027 campaign at Ekwueme Square, Awka. According to him, APGA has no presidential candidate for the 2027 general election and would, therefore, adopt President Tinubu as its preferred candidate. “Today, we adopt the APC presidential candidate, Bola Ahmed Tinubu as our candidate,” he declared, noting that the president had demonstrated love and concern for the Igbo people, particularly the people of Anambra State. The governor recalled that the President had appointed several Anambra indigenes to strategic positions in Lagos State during his tenure as governor. He also recalled that APGA had adopted the presidential candidate of the ruling party in previous elections, noting that the party’s decision to support Tinubu in 2027 was a continuation of that political arrangement that had been in existence. He lamented that Anambra State recorded fewer than 5,000 votes for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, yet the President has continued to address some of the challenges confronting the state and the South-East region. He urged the Anambra electorate to support Tinubu in the 2027 election, arguing that doing so would give the state and the South-East a stronger opportunity to engage with the Federal Government and negotiate for their development. “We need to vote for him in order to sit with the government at the centre and negotiate for the development of the South-East and Anambra State”, he declared. item.description: Washington is offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. Read Also: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X. The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges. It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward. Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear program. “If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.” But the president also said Iran – which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war – is eager to end the conflict. “We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said. Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting. And on Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue. Earlier this week Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. The inauguration took place on November 16, 1960, at Tafawa Balewa Square, barely six weeks after independence. It was also Zik’s 56th birthday. item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, who disclosed this on Friday while presenting the Command’s operational scorecard, said the arrests followed intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies. On the Uratta police station attack, Afolabi said investigations had led to the arrest of some of the suspected attackers, with one of them allegedly confessing to leading the gang that carried out the assault. He said investigations were ongoing to track down other accomplices and establish the full circumstances surrounding the attack. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. The children were reportedly recovered and handed back to their parents, while the suspects were charged to court. The police boss also announced the arrest of a five-man vehicle theft syndicate, aged 43, and 40. A Toyota Corolla with registration number ROU 9338J was recovered from the suspects, who have also been charged to court. In another operation, two suspected cultists, aged 27, and 25, were arrested on October 31 for allegedly dispossessing students of Abia State University, Uturu, of their mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint. item.title: ‘Sort out your internal mess’, APC tells Atiku, ADC after court judgment
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The All Progressives Congress APC has told the Senator David Mark-led faction of the African Democratic Congress ADC to go sort out its internal mess and quit its “senseless rants” after a Federal High Court judgment sacked the faction’s leadership. Read Also: ADC Crisis: What becomes of Atiku, Mark, Gombe if Supreme Court decides party’s fate? In a statement Friday in Abuja, the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said the ruling party had no hand in the case. “To be clear, APC is neither a party nor an interlocutor in the matter. Nothing about the case has anything to do with the APC. And the APC has absolutely no role in the party’s judicial quagmire,” he said. The judgment, delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, sacked the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC. It also nullified all official acts of that leadership, including its primary election processes and outcomes, like the presidential candidacy of former vice president Atiku Abubakar. Morka said the case was brought by ADC national officers against the faction now removed from office, describing the suit as “a notorious case initiated by leaders of ADC against pirate leaders of ADC.” He accused Mark and his associates of taking over the party “to satisfy Atiku Abubakar’s quixotic presidential ambition.” According to him, “it didn’t matter to them that their hostile takeover of that party was in flagrant violation of the rule of law and ADC’s internal democracy, as a court of competent jurisdiction has now declared.” The APC spokesman also accused the ADC of reacting to court decisions according to whether they favour it. “Every time a court decides against the Senator David Mark-led factional African Democratic Congress, they accuse the All Progressives Congress of collusion and deprecate the judiciary. Every time a court decides in their favour, they hail the rule of law and extol the judiciary,” he said. He added that the faction’s attitude showed “no iota of regard for the authority and independence of the judiciary, an indispensable pillar of any democracy.” On Thursday’s ruling, Morka said it “was procured by their own lawlessness and demonstrates the vibrancy of the rule of law and independence of the judiciary in Nigeria.” He said the ADC leaders “take no responsibility or accountability for the self-inflicted injury that the court only judicially certified.” Vanguard News The post ‘Sort out your internal mess’, APC tells Atiku, ADC after court judgment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Scientists turn cancer cells into weapons against tumours
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe What if the chemical produced in abundance by cancer cells could be turned against the cancers? What if, instead of flooding the entire body with powerful drugs in an attempt to destroy a tumour, scientists could persuade cancer cells to manufacture destructive chemicals from within? That possibility is at the centre of an intriguing scientific breakthrough in Japan, where researchers have developed an experimental technique that exploits carbon monoxide produced by cancer cells to generate cancer-killing compounds inside them. The approach turns an unusual feature of cancer biology into a potential therapeutic advantage. Rather than administering an already manufactured toxic drug that circulates through the body and can damage healthy tissues, the researchers have devised a chemical system that produces an anticancer compound inside targeted cancer cells. In laboratory experiments, the technique successfully generated toxic compounds in several cancer cell lines while leaving a noncancerous cell line without detectable production of the same compound. Although still at an early experimental stage, the findings could open a new direction in cancer treatment, particularly in the long-standing search for ways to destroy malignant cells while sparing healthy tissues from the collateral damage associated with conventional chemotherapy. The research, led by Katsunori Tanaka at the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), Japan, was published in Nature Communications. Cancer treatment has long been complicated by a fundamental problem: drugs powerful enough to destroy malignant cells can also injure normal cells. Chemotherapy, for instance, often affects healthy tissues because many anticancer medicines cannot distinguish perfectly between cancerous and noncancerous cells. The resulting damage can produce debilitating side effects, including nausea, fatigue, hair loss and suppression of the immune system. Scientists have consequently been exploring more selective ways of delivering or generating anticancer agents at the precise location where they are needed. Tanaka and colleagues focused on carbon monoxide, a gas commonly recognised for its toxicity but also naturally produced in small quantities in the human body. Their strategy was to deliver a metal-based catalyst into cells and use the available carbon monoxide as the chemical fuel for a reaction that manufactures an anticancer substance. In principle, the reaction would be activated predominantly in cancer cells, where sufficient carbon monoxide is available, rather than in healthy tissues. The research represents part of a developing scientific field known as therapeutic in vivo synthetic chemistry, which seeks to use chemical reactions inside living organisms to manufacture therapeutic substances where they are needed. When a trader gets the right spectacles, she keeps her business alive. When a child can see clearly, her education improves. When an older person regains independence, a family recovers hours once spent on caregiving; hours that can be used to work, study and earn. item.description: President Bola Tinubu said that Naira would have been so worthless, it would be moved about by wheelbarrow if not for his economic policies that moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ Tinubu, the presidential candidate of All Progressives Congress, APC, said this during his visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters to support his administration and Governor Umo Eno. He described the January 16, 2027 election as consequential, saying it would determine the country’s direction. Defending his economic policies, Tinubu said his administration had moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. According to him, “This coming election, on January 16th is a consequential election. It will define the direction of this country. “When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary, not to talk of pension, and gratuity. Today, I can say that we are out of that tunnel. “And I can beat my chest to say we are out of the despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of a possible bankruptcy. “By now if we didn’t take over, if we didn’t do what we did, we will be using the wheelbarrows to move our naira about because it will have become valueless.” On young voters The President urged the electorate, particularly young people, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described it as their most potent instrument for determining the country’s political future. At a reception held in his honour at Ibom Palm Resort, Tinubu praised Eno. He described the resort as evidence of purposeful leadership and the possibility of reclaiming environmentally degraded land for productive use. “We are standing on a resort to the glory of God. It is a product of 73 acres of land of gully erosion, reclaimed, surrounded with a good, romantic, artificial lake, demonstrating a serious vision that is achievable when honest people are working for their homes,” he said. item.title: ADC Crisis: What becomes of Atiku, Mark, Gombe if Supreme Court decides party’s fate?
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress (ADC) was meant to be the meeting point of opposition forces determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Instead, the party has become the battleground for a struggle that could undo the coalition it was expected to accommodate. Read Also: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy Barely 24 hours after former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar took his presidential campaign to Sokoto, a Federal High Court judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu threw the party into fresh uncertainty, nullifying the David Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under it, including the process that produced Atiku as presidential candidate. For Mark and his allies, it was a setback at a critical moment. For Nafiu Bala Gombe, who challenged the leadership transition, it was a victory in a battle he had refused to abandon. For Atiku, it was a reminder that the platform on which he hopes to return to Aso Rock may not be entirely within his control. With the Mark faction preparing to appeal, attention is shifting to the appellate courts. Whatever the eventual outcome, the political fortunes of some of the coalition’s most prominent figures are at stake. How it all began The dispute began when former ADC National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, facilitated a leadership transition that brought Mark and former Osun State Governor, Rauf Aregbesola, into the party as National Chairman and National Secretary respectively. The arrangement offered opposition politicians an existing political structure around which to build a challenge to the APC. But Gombe, a former Deputy National Chairman, North, objected, arguing that the party’s constitution provided a succession procedure that was not followed. His challenge produced Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment. The Mark faction, however, insists that the leadership question had already been examined by the court. It points to the July 2, 2026, judgment of Justice Musa Liman in a separate suit instituted by House of Representatives member Leke Abejide. Justice Liman upheld preliminary objections, including lack of jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies. He also made findings favourable to the defendants concerning the leadership transition The Mark camp argues that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot overturn another court’s decision. The Supreme Court had intervened on April 30, setting aside an earlier status quo ante bellum order and directing an expedited hearing at the Federal High Court. It did not decide who was entitled to lead the ADC While Mark’s camp rejects the latest judgment, Gombe has celebrated it as a victory for constitutional governance. “Political parties are not above their own constitutions, and the Electoral Act is not a mere suggestion,” he declared. If Gombe wins at S-Court, where does Atiku go? A final Supreme Court victory for Gombe could leave Atiku facing a difficult political calculation. If the court upholds the nullification of the Mark-led leadership and its consequential decisions, the former Vice-President’s presidential nomination could become legally untenable. His political influence would remain, but finding another viable platform at this stage would be difficult. Atiku has made clear that he intends to fight the judgment. “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. A Gombe victory at the apex court would also cost Mark and Aregbesola their positions and potentially undermine the machinery through which the coalition intends to contest the elections. The consequences could extend to governorship, Senate, House of Representatives and State Assembly candidates whose nominations were made under the disputed leadership. Their electoral ambitions could be affected if the final orders invalidate those nominations. For Gombe, however, winning the chairmanship would not automatically mean inheriting the coalition’s political networks, resources and prominent figures. He would have to decide whether to accommodate the politicians who joined under Mark or risk a party weakened by their departure. Nwosu would equally face renewed questions about the leadership transition he facilitated, although a judgment against Mark’s structure would not automatically establish personal wrongdoing on his part. If Mark wins at S-Court, Gombe faces another choice A final victory for Mark would preserve the coalition’s leadership structure, strengthen the position of existing ADC candidates and remove the immediate legal threat to Atiku’s ticket. Aregbesola would retain his position, while Atiku could concentrate on his campaign rather than spend valuable time defending his political platform. Rotimi Amaechi, his presidential running mate, and other candidates would also have greater certainty over their nominations. Gombe, meanwhile, would have to decide whether to remain in the party, accept the coalition’s leadership or seek another political arrangement. His influence would depend on the support he retains among the ADC’s original membership. But a Mark victory would not automatically end the internal struggle. The coalition brings together politicians with different ambitions and constituencies. Their common opposition to Tinubu does not mean they agree on the distribution of party offices, influence and political opportunities. Mark would still have to demonstrate that the ADC can function as a political party rather than an alliance held together principally by the desire to challenge the APC. The election clock is ticking The electoral timetable makes the dispute particularly consequential. INEC has scheduled the presidential and National Assembly elections for January 16, 2027, and governorship and State Assembly elections for February 6. The deadlines for party primaries and replacement of presidential candidates have passed. Consequently, a Gombe victory would not automatically give the recognised leadership an opportunity to conduct fresh primaries and nominate new candidates. Whether existing nominations survive would depend on the final appellate orders, their scope and the applicable electoral provisions. For thousands of candidates, the dispute is no longer simply an argument between political heavyweights in Abuja. It is about whether their names will remain on the ballot after months of campaigning. The ADC has accused the APC of exploiting the crisis to weaken the opposition. The ruling party has denied involvement, describing the matter as an internal ADC dispute. Those allegations remain contested. Ultimately, the Supreme Court may determine who legally controls the ADC, but it cannot guarantee that the victorious faction will retain the loyalty of the coalition. If Gombe wins, he could secure the party but struggle to retain the coalition. If Mark wins, he could preserve the coalition’s platform but still face the task of reconciling an aggrieved original membership. For Atiku, the immediate question is whether his presidential ambition can survive the loss of its chosen platform. item.title: ‘Our fathers have spoken’- Middle Belt youths rally behind Tinubu
item.description: Youths from the Middle Belt have declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, announcing plans to mobilise voters across the region for the All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group said it would work with the City Boy Movement, led by Seyi Tinubu, its Director-General, Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, and the APC campaign council to coordinate the mobilisation. The initiative is being championed by aviation entrepreneur and political figure, Isaac Balami, who said the decision followed a meeting between Tinubu and prominent Middle Belt leaders led by elder statesman, General Theophilus Yakubu Danjuma. Balami described the engagement at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, as a turning point for the region, saying younger people were ready to follow the political direction established by their elders. “Our fathers have spoken. They have met the father. We have equally met the son. The movement has begun,” he said. Balami recalled that the same elders had asked him to mobilise support for Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi in the 2023 election. He said a fallout over what he described as abandonment had contributed to the latest political realignment. The founder of the National Rebirth Movement, who also serves as an executive board member and National Director on Special Duty of the City Boy Movement, said the decision to support Tinubu was informed by the region’s representation in the administration. He cited appointments to strategic government positions, efforts to tackle insecurity and the inclusion of Middle Belt representatives in national decision-making. “We have people from our region occupying important positions in this government. For us as young people, representation matters,” Balami said. He said the group would mobilise across the Middle Belt, adding that some youths who supported Obi in 2023 were now prepared to back Tinubu. Balami also identified security, infrastructure, education, employment and economic opportunities as issues requiring sustained government attention. He said the movement aimed to involve young people in political decisions affecting the region rather than limit their participation to election campaigns. The announcement follows Thursday’s meeting between Tinubu and a delegation of Middle Belt and North-Central leaders led by Danjuma. The delegation included Defence Minister Christopher Musa, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang, Taraba State Governor Agbu Kefas, former House of Representatives Speaker Yakubu Dogara and former Chief of Army Staff General Ishaya Bamaiyi. Dogara said the delegation met Tinubu to express solidarity with his administration and discuss security, development and political engagement ahead of the 2027 elections. The emerging youth mobilisation signals an effort to translate the engagement of regional elders into electoral support for Tinubu in an area where Obi secured considerable backing in 2023. The opposition should learn a thing or two from the Democrats who were laser focused on the economy. The incumbent on the other hand is street smart. He is like a chess player who knows the weaknesses of his opponent. He also has the resources financially and coercively, to sway the polls in his favor. And as long as opposition continues to play the game along tribal, ‘emilokan’ lines, as long as solutions to issues that affect the working class are not focused on, the incumbent would have the day come January 16. The so called ‘obidients’ for example, are not likely to win more independent souls with their aggressive and abusive approach to dissent. If your principal has some strengths – and he does – then articulate them. If he has antecedents in words and deeds that can promote a more united and more economically buoyant country, then articulate them. Stop attacking dissent. It is not the best way to win new friends. The President’s Achilles heel in this election is the economy. Not necessarily the fundamentals which he had tried to correct through the reforms and on which many think he has scored a pass mark – at least, they have stabilized the economy. But in the attendant fall-out from the reforms which in his haste and hubris, he failed to correctly address. I use the words ‘haste’ and ‘hubris’ advisedly. No serious economist or public commentator would question the need for the reforms. The reforms were long overdue because we were running a dysfunctional economy. But the way they were handled can easily turn a hero into a villain. A bit of sensitivity, a bit of time to cross the ‘Ts’ and dot the ‘I’ could have made a difference. A more empathetic approach to the suffering of the people could have made a difference. That is haste that could have been better managed. Many Nigerians have dropped into the poverty zone. The US led war against Iran has not helped matters. Almost all Nigerians have received severe knocks on their quality of life. I say almost because the political class, led by the Presidency, still behaves as if it is from Mars. That is part of the hubris of power. The lack of adequate safety nets for the most vulnerable in the society is a minus for a President who thinks he knows Nigeria. The opposition can turn the tide and make the next few weeks preceding the election uncomfortable for the incumbent if it can focus on affordability issues and the rising cost of living. But it has to show that it has a better alternative beyond rhetoric. It is not by introducing dysfunctional, badly thought out subsidies which could take us back in time. Nigerians don’t want to suffer the pains of the last three years in vain. We need a solid economic blueprint which should take Nigeria to the next level among the comity of nations. The opposition needs to succeed where the incumbent has failed which is to connect with the people in meaningful ways. But first, it has to come together to speak with one voice. Then, it has to articulate its economic direction in more meaningful ways. The post January 2027: Tinubu’s achilles heel, by Muyiwa Adetiba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: Hundreds of youths in Ebonyi State have staged a peaceful march through Abakaliki, the state capital, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said they came from the 13 local government areas of the state to demand a peaceful political atmosphere in which all citizens can participate without fear. The demonstrators marched through major streets in Abakaliki, displaying placards with messages including, “Democracy Needs Peaceful Ideas, Not Weapons” and “Protect Freedom of Speech in Ebonyi.” Addressing journalists during the rally, a spokesperson for the group said the youths would not accept any attempt to undermine their constitutional rights. “Our constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly are not negotiable,” the spokesperson said. The group also expressed concern over reported incidents of physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation targeting opposition figures in parts of the state. “We will not sit by while political thuggery and intimidation threaten to ruin our state’s democratic process. Every citizen, regardless of party alignment, deserves to participate without fear for their safety,” the spokesperson added. The protesters called on security agencies and state institutions to intervene and ensure a level playing field for all political parties. Another youth coordinator said opposition parties should be able to campaign, present their programmes and engage voters without threats or intimidation. “Opposition parties must be allowed to campaign safely, present their platforms, and engage with voters without constant threat of violence,” the coordinator said. The group said the march was part of efforts by young people in the state to demand accountability and promote peaceful political participation as the 2027 general elections approach.
